stem: Which account is reconstructed to find a trader's **credit sales** for the year?

options.rationale: Correct: credit sales are debited to this account.
This account gives credit purchases.
The capital account records the owner's investment, profit and drawings.
This records goods returned by customers only.

explanation: Credit sales increase what customers owe, so they are the missing debit in the total trade receivables account.

stem: In a total trade payables account, on which side is **discount received** entered?

options.content: Debit, because it reduces the amount owed to suppliers
options.rationale: Correct: it lowers the liability.

options.content: Credit, because it is income of the business
options.rationale: In the discount received account it is a credit; in the payables account it is a debit.
Discount received does not change purchases.

options.content: It is not entered in the trade payables account
options.rationale: It reduces the suppliers' balances, so it must appear.

explanation: Discount received reduces the amount owed to suppliers, so the payables account is debited and discount received credited.

stem: Trade receivables were US\$2,870 on 1 January 2025 and US\$3,150 on 31 December 2025. Customers paid US\$35,640 and were allowed discounts of US\$410. What were the credit sales?

options.rationale: The opening and closing balances have been swapped.
The discount has been deducted instead of added.
Cash received is not the same as credit sales.

explanation: Credit sales = receipts + discount allowed + closing − opening = 35,640 + 410 + 3,150 − 2,870 = 36,330.

stem: Trade payables: 1 January US\$4,120; 31 December US\$3,780. Paid to suppliers US\$52,300; discount received US\$720; purchases returns US\$1,140. What were the credit purchases?

options.rationale: Purchases returns have been deducted instead of added.
Discount received and returns have been left out.
The opening and closing balances have been swapped.

hints: Everything on the debit side of the payables account is added; the opening balance is deducted.

stem: During 2025 Rudo paid US\$2,760 for electricity. At 1 January US\$180 was owing and at 31 December US\$230 was owing. What is the electricity expense for 2025?

options.rationale: The opening accrual belongs to 2024 and must be deducted.
The accruals have been treated the wrong way round.
The amount paid has not been adjusted for accruals.

explanation: Expense = paid − opening accrual + closing accrual = 2,760 − 180 + 230 = 2,810.

stem: Insurance paid during 2025 was US\$4,800. Insurance prepaid was US\$400 at 1 January and US\$600 at 31 December. What is the insurance expense for 2025?

options.rationale: The prepayments have been treated as accruals.
The closing prepayment belongs to 2026 and must be deducted.
The opening prepayment was used in 2025 and must be added.

hints: An opening prepayment is used up this year; a closing prepayment belongs to next year.

stem: Sipho's bank balance was US\$1,240 at the start of the year and US\$980 at the end. Receipts were US\$27,400 and business payments US\$24,960. All other withdrawals were drawings. How much did he draw?

options.rationale: The opening and closing balances have been ignored.
The closing balance has been added instead of deducted.
The opening balance has been left out.

explanation: Money available 28,640; less payments 24,960 and closing balance 980 leaves drawings of 2,700.

stem: A trader paid her rent for January 2026 in December 2025. Ignoring this when finding the 2025 rent expense from the bank summary would …

options.content: understate the rent expense and overstate profit
options.rationale: The extra payment increases the expense if not adjusted.

options.content: overstate the rent expense and understate profit
options.rationale: Correct: next year's rent would be charged to 2025.

options.content: have no effect on profit, only on the bank balance
options.rationale: The expense, and so the profit, would be wrong.

options.content: overstate both the rent expense and the profit
options.rationale: A larger expense lowers profit.

explanation: The payment in advance is a closing prepayment. Unless it is deducted, the 2025 expense is too high and the profit too low.
hints: The January 2026 rent is a closing prepayment.

stem: Which item is entered on the **credit** side of a total trade receivables account?

options.rationale: Credit sales are debited: they increase what customers owe.
The opening balance is a debit balance b/d.
Correct: they reduce the amount customers owe.
A dishonoured cheque restores the debt, so it is debited.

explanation: Receipts, discount allowed, sales returns, irrecoverable debts and contras reduce receivables and are credits.

stem: Total revenue for the year is cash sales plus credit sales.
explanation: True. The receivables account gives credit sales only; cash sales are added to give total revenue.

stem: The amount received from credit customers during the year is always equal to credit sales for the year.
explanation: False. Receipts include payment for last year's sales and exclude sales still unpaid at the year end, discounts and returns.

stem: Match each missing figure with the account usually reconstructed to find it.

left.content: Rent charged in the income statement
Cash sales (takings not banked in full)

explanation: Each figure is the missing entry in the account it would have been posted to.

stem: Complete the formula for credit purchases.

payload.template: Credit purchases = payments to suppliers + discount received + purchases returns + {{blank:a}} trade payables − {{blank:b}} trade payables.

explanation: Closing payables are the balance c/d on the debit side; the opening balance b/d on the credit side is deducted.

stem: Farai's hardware shop in Gweru: trade receivables US\$5,260 at 1 January 2025 and US\$6,040 at 31 December 2025. During 2025 customers paid US\$61,480; discount allowed was US\$870; sales returns US\$1,320; irrecoverable debts written off US\$640. Cash sales were US\$9,350. Calculate the total revenue (sales) for 2025.
explanation: Credit sales = 61,480 + 870 + 1,320 + 640 + 6,040 − 5,260 = 65,090. Revenue = 65,090 + 9,350 = 74,440. Forgetting the cash sales gives 65,090; using receipts as credit sales gives 70,830.
workedSolution: 1. Credit sales = 61,480 + 870 + 1,320 + 640 + 6,040 − 5,260 = 65,090. Revenue = 65,090 + 9,350 = 74,440. Forgetting the cash sales gives 65,090; using receipts as credit sales gives 70,830.
hints: Find credit sales from the receivables account first.

stem: Nyasha's trade payables were US\$2,380 on 1 January 2025. Credit purchases for the year were US\$28,740, she paid suppliers US\$27,150 and received discounts of US\$450. Calculate her trade payables at 31 December 2025.
explanation: Closing payables = 2,380 + 28,740 − 27,150 − 450 = 3,520. Forgetting the discount gives 3,970.
workedSolution: 1. Closing payables = 2,380 + 28,740 − 27,150 − 450 = 3,520. Forgetting the discount gives 3,970.
hints: This time the balance c/d is the missing figure.

stem: Chipo runs a market stall in Mbare. All her sales are for cash. During 2025 she banked US\$31,600 of takings, paid a helper's wages of US\$2,880 out of the takings and took US\$1,500 from the takings for herself. Cash in hand was US\$160 at 1 January and US\$245 at 31 December 2025. Calculate her cash sales for 2025.
explanation: Cash sales = banked 31,600 + wages 2,880 + drawings 1,500 + closing cash 245 − opening cash 160 = 36,065. Using only the amount banked (31,600) ignores everything spent from the till.
workedSolution: 1. Cash sales = banked 31,600 + wages 2,880 + drawings 1,500 + closing cash 245 − opening cash 160 = 36,065. Using only the amount banked (31,600) ignores everything spent from the till.
hints: Cash sales are the missing receipt in a cash summary.
Everything paid out of the takings, plus the closing cash, came from opening cash and sales.

stem: Explain why the amount paid for rent during the year may differ from the rent expense in the income statement.

points.description: Some rent may be owing (accrued) or paid in advance (prepaid) at the start or end of the year
The expense must match the rent for the year's use only (accruals/matching concept)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Part of the payments may cover next year (a prepayment) or last year's arrears, and rent for this year may still be owing. The income statement must show only the rent for the period used this year.

explanation: Accruals concept: expenses are matched to the period they relate to.

stem: A trader's total trade receivables account gives credit sales of US\$40,000, but she has forgotten to tell her accountant about irrecoverable debts of US\$700. State and explain the effect on the credit sales calculated.

points.description: Credit sales are understated by US\$700
Irrecoverable debts are a credit in the account; leaving them out makes the missing debit (credit sales) too small

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Credit sales will be understated by US\$700 (they should be US\$40,700), because the debts written off are a credit entry and the missing figure on the debit side has to cover them.

explanation: Every credit omitted reduces the calculated debit missing figure by the same amount.
hints: Which side are irrecoverable debts on, and which side is the missing figure on?
